claim: Consider a two-row ecological abundance table with \(k\ge2\) labeled species, strictly positive integer counts \(x=(x_1,\ldots,x_k)\) and \(y=(y_1,\ldots,y_k)\), and equal row totals \(\sum_i x_i=\sum_i y_i=N\). Let Bray–Curtis dissimilarity be \(B(x,y)=\frac{1}{2N}\sum_i|x_i-y_i|\), and let \(X(x,y)\) be the ordinary correspondence-analysis chi-square distance between the two row profiles, with column masses computed from this two-row table. Then \(X(x,y)^2=\frac{2}{N}\sum_i (x_i-y_i)^2/(x_i+y_i)\). For every \(N\le9\) and every admissible \(k\), no two such tables with the same \((N,k)\) receive opposite strict orderings from \(B\) and \(X\). At \(N=10\), strict reversal occurs for the first time, and richness \(k=3\) is sufficient and minimal within that first layer. The pair \(x=(1,3,6),y=(3,1,6)\) has \(B=1/5\) and \(X^2=2/5\), whereas \(u=(1,2,7),v=(2,4,4)\) has \(B=3/10\) and \(X^2=4/11\); hence Bray–Curtis judges the second pair more dissimilar while chi-square distance judges the first pair more dissimilar. At \(N=10\), reversals occur exactly for \(k\in\{3,4,5,6\}\).
integrity: The formulas are derived from the definitions. Exhaustive finite verification generates every positive composition and every unordered community pair through the sharp census, using exact rational arithmetic and combinatorial cardinality checks.
scientific_limitations: Strictly positive integer abundances, equal row totals, and chi-square column masses computed from the same two-row table are required. Zero counts, larger background tables, and sampling uncertainty are outside scope.
title: Ten individuals are the sharp equal-census Bray–Curtis–chi-square reversal boundary
